title: Kong and Straiker add runtime protection and containment for AI agents
summary: The integration extends Kong AI Gateway from traffic governance into a complementary security loop spanning agent discovery, adversarial testing, runtime verdicts, inline enforcement, and agent-level containment. It strengthens Kong's regulated-enterprise positioning, but does not change the thesis score because no adoption, bookings, pricing, or revenue contribution was disclosed.
confirmed: Kong and Straiker announced an integration in which Straiker evaluates configured LLM, MCP/tool, and agent-to-agent traffic and returns security decisions for Kong AI Gateway to enforce.
The companies describe escalation beyond blocking one request to agent-level containment, including revoking tools, suspending sessions, freezing memory, or taking an agent or agent fleet offline.
Both companies say the integration is designed for existing Kong-routed production workflows and cite customer deployments or active proofs of value in regulated industries.
uncertain: No joint-customer count, named deployment, product availability tier, pricing, attach rate, contractual economics, bookings, ARR, or revenue contribution was disclosed.
Straiker's detection-performance figures are vendor-reported and were not independently validated in the announcement.
